findings.title: Unguarded access to destructured destinationCalendar causes TypeError
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` (no optional chaining) will throw a TypeError whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is empty/undefined (a very common case – e.g. no connected calendar) and the location is Google Meet. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was safe. This regression will crash booking creation whenever Google Meet is selected as the location and there is no destination calendar set, instead of correctly falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Broken calendarId fallback logic in updateEvent
findings.body: `selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` – the fallback branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it still searches `destinationCalendar` for an entry whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value, which will essentially never match. Previously the fallback correctly used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (the main calendar). Now `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` whenever no externalCalendarId is supplied (e.g. legacy bookings without a stored externalCalendarId), and `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`, which will fail against the Google API.

findings.title: Broken calendarId fallback logic in deleteEvent defaults to 'primary'
findings.body: Same faulty pattern as updateEvent: `calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` always resolves to `undefined` when `externalCalendarId` isn't supplied, so `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` falls back to `"primary"` instead of the correct destination calendar. This can cause deleteEvent to delete (or attempt to delete) an event from the wrong calendar (the user's primary calendar) instead of the actual destination calendar, leaving the real event un-cancelled – a data-integrity risk for cancellations/reschedules of bookings lacking a stored externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Team destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (which happens whenever neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set). In that scenario, for a COLLECTIVE event, the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` for the other hosts are silently discarded and never pushed into `evt.destinationCalendar`, meaning other hosts' calendars will not receive the event — defeating the primary purpose of this PR (handling collective events with multiple hosts).

findings.title: Office365/Lark/CalDAV calendar services ignore credentialId and always use first destinationCalendar entry
findings.body: Unlike googlecalendar's createEvent, which now selects the correct calendar via `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, Office365 (and similarly Lark and the base CalDAV service) continue to use only `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` (the first array entry) regardless of which credential/host is currently being processed by EventManager's per-destination loop. As a result, when a collective event has hosts using Office365/Lark/CalDAV calendars, the event will be repeatedly created against the *same* (first) host's calendar instead of each host's own calendar, so the multi-host destination-calendar fix only actually works for Google Calendar.

findings.title: Inverted conditional logic for organization slug assignment, unrelated to stated PR scope
findings.body: The condition for setting `slug` on org creation was flipped: originally `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` (slug set when team billing is disabled) is now `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (slug set when team billing is enabled). This behavior change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (destinationCalendar array handling) and appears to be an accidental regression that changes when an organization's slug is persisted at creation time.

findings.title: Dynamic-user lookup no longer selects organization slug
findings.body: In the refactored `loadUsers`, the `prisma.user.findMany` query for the dynamic-booking (`!eventTypeId`) branch no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, which was present before this change. If any downstream code (e.g. building dynamic group booking URLs, org-aware redirects) relies on `user.organization.slug` for these users, it will now be `undefined`, silently breaking organization-aware behavior for dynamic group bookings.

findings.title: Inconsistent and incomplete test coverage for destinationCalendar shape change
findings.body: Only the BOOKING_REJECTED test was updated to expect `destinationCalendar: []` while BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests (lines 119 and 373) still assert `destinationCalendar: null`. This reflects a real inconsistency in the codebase (some code paths emit `null`, others emit `[]`) but no test actually exercises the PR's stated goal — a collective event with multiple hosts receiving correctly populated destinationCalendar arrays. The PR explicitly acknowledges no tests were added for the core fix.

findings.title: References built from result.externalId/credentialId lose fallback to evt.destinationCalendar for video-only results
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` now uses `isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` and `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` instead of previously falling back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`/`credentialId` for non-calendar (video) results. Since `destinationCalendar` is now an array, the previous single-value fallback was removed entirely rather than adapted (e.g. to the first entry), silently dropping any externalCalendarId/credentialId info for video event references which previously could inherit it from the destination calendar.
